evals.name: jsp-gurobi-to-cpsat
evals.prompt: ジョブショップスケジューリング (n=20 jobs × m=10 machines、makespan 最小化) を Gurobi で書いてみたんですが、disjunctive 制約の Big-M を job 総処理時間の和に取ったら、20分回しても optimality gap が 50% 以上残ります。何か根本的に手法を変えるべきでしょうか？
evals.expected_output: CP-SAT (OR-Tools) への切替を最優先で提案。IntervalVar + AddNoOverlap の構文例。MiniZinc Challenge 2019-2024連続全部門金メダルの根拠。num_search_workers=8 などの portfolio 並列。CP-SAT は整数係数のみなのでスケーリング注意。Ku & Beck 2016 で disjunctive が MIP の中では最良という背景も触れられると良い。Big-M をタイト化する話だけで終わらない (CP-SAT 切替の方が根本的)。
assertions: Recommends switching to CP-SAT (OR-Tools) as the primary fix, not merely tightening Big-M
Shows an IntervalVar + AddNoOverlap CP-SAT snippet
Mentions CP-SAT integer-only coefficients and the need to scale real values
Cites MiniZinc Challenge results and/or Ku & Beck 2016 as evidence
Mentions num_search_workers / portfolio parallelism

evals.name: ufl-weak-formulation
evals.prompt: 施設配置問題 (UFL, |I|=200 顧客、|J|=50 候補施設) を Gurobi で解いています。"Σᵢ xᵢⱼ ≤ |I|·yⱼ" という制約を |J| 本書いて LP relaxation を取ったら root gap が 40% もあり、分枝木が爆発します。formulation 自体に問題がありますか？
evals.expected_output: 弱い formulation (集約形) を強い formulation (分散形 xᵢⱼ ≤ yⱼ ∀i,j) に書き換えることを最優先で提案。UFL では分散形だと LP relaxation が integer optimal を出すことが多い点。制約数は |I|·|J|=10000 に増えるが presolve で削減されること。Capacitated FL の場合は flow cover cuts や Benders 分解の話も触れられると良い。modeling-techniques.md §1 と problem-catalog.md §6.1 の知識を統合して回答できているか。
assertions: Identifies the aggregated constraint as a weak formulation and recommends the disaggregated form xij <= yj for all i,j
Explains the disaggregated UFL LP relaxation is often integer-optimal / much tighter
Notes the constraint count grows to |I|*|J| but presolve mitigates it
Mentions a capacitated-FL path (flow cover cuts or Benders) as a caveat

evals.name: vrp-exact-vs-heuristic
evals.prompt: CVRPTW (顧客 300、デポ 1、車両 30、時間窓あり) を Gurobi の MIP で 3-index 定式化で書いてみたら、24時間回しても実行可能解すら出ません。実務では夜間バッチ 4時間で解きたいです。どうアプローチを変えるべきですか？
evals.expected_output: 実務サイズ VRPTW を exact MIP で解くのは現実的でない、と明示。代替手法を複数提示すべき: (a) OR-Tools Routing solver, (b) HGS-CVRP/HGS 系, (c) ALNS (Ropke-Pisinger 2006), (d) Branch-and-Price は exact 寄りだが実装重い。第一推奨は OR-Tools Routing。Solomon benchmark や CVRPLIB の情報も触れる。"Gurobi で 24時間" を放置して頑張る方向のアドバイスは NG。
assertions: States plainly that exact MIP is impractical at this scale and stops recommending the 24h Gurobi path
Offers multiple heuristic/metaheuristic alternatives (at least OR-Tools Routing plus one of HGS-CVRP / ALNS)
Names OR-Tools Routing as a first practical recommendation
References a benchmark/library (Solomon or CVRPLIB)

evals.name: route-to-iis-skill
evals.prompt: My production scheduling model is coming back INFEASIBLE from Gurobi and I have no idea which constraints are fighting each other. I've attached the model as schedule.lp. Can you figure out why it won't solve and what I'd need to change in the input data to make it feasible?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that a concrete .lp file + infeasibility is exactly the iis-summarization skill's job and route there first, rather than only theorizing. Then layer modeling judgment: once the IIS names conflicting constraints, question the hard/soft classification (Principle 8) before relaxing anything. Should NOT just give generic 'check your constraints' advice while ignoring that an actual model file was provided.
assertions: Routes to / hands off to the iis-summarization skill because a concrete .lp file plus infeasibility was provided
Does not merely give generic advice while ignoring the attached model file
Brings in the hard-vs-soft constraint judgment (question which conflicting constraint is truly hard before relaxing)

evals.name: bigm-review-numerical
evals.prompt: Can you review this MILP before I scale it up? It's a facility-siting model. The disjunctive constraints all use M = 1e7, and I mix dollar costs (~1e6) with CO2 coefficients (~0.0005) in the same constraints. It solves on toy data but I'm nervous about the full instance.
evals.expected_output: Should flag two distinct problems: (1) the un-tightened Big-M = 1e7 (derive M from tightened bounds, or use indicator/SOS1), and (2) the coefficient range spanning ~1e6 to ~5e-4 (ratio ~2e9) which risks numerical instability and should be rescaled into roughly [1e-6, 1e6]. Bonus: suggests running lp_scan.py on the exported model file for an objective pre-solve check. Cites the relevant antipattern/modeling-technique sections.
assertions: Flags the Big-M = 1e7 as un-tightened and recommends deriving M from bounds or using indicator/SOS1 constraints
Flags the wide coefficient range (dollars ~1e6 vs CO2 ~5e-4) as a numerical-conditioning risk and recommends rescaling
Mentions the lp_scan.py pre-solve check or otherwise grounds the review in an objective scan
Cites relevant references (Big-M design / numerical stability / antipatterns)

evals.name: socratic-vague-business-problem
evals.prompt: Hi! I run operations for a mid-size meal-kit company. Our delivery and warehouse costs feel way too high and scheduling is chaos. I've heard 'optimization' can help but honestly I don't even know where to start or what's possible. Can you help?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT immediately dump a generic MIP/VRP tutorial. Instead behaves as a Socratic advisor: asks a small batch (2-4) of focused diagnostic questions to identify the actual optimization problem(s) — what decisions they control, what 'better' means (objective), what rules are hard vs preferences, scale, time/data available — and explains briefly why it's asking. Likely surfaces that there may be multiple sub-problems (routing vs warehouse staffing vs inventory) and proposes scoping one first. Offers to restate the problem back once answered. Keeps it approachable (non-expert user), not a wall of jargon.
assertions: Asks a focused batch (roughly 2-4) of diagnostic questions rather than dumping a generic solution
Questions aim to extract decisions / objective / constraints (problem identification), not just solver trivia
Recognizes there may be multiple distinct sub-problems and suggests scoping/prioritizing one
Briefly explains why it is asking and keeps the tone approachable for a non-expert
Does not prematurely commit to a specific solver or formulation before the basics are known

evals.name: gurobipy-conditional-code
evals.prompt: In gurobipy I have a binary b and a continuous variable x in [0, 200]. I want a variable z that equals b*x (so z=0 when b=0, z=x when b=1). I tried z == b*x and Gurobi complained it's nonlinear. What's the right way, and should I worry about Big-M here?
evals.expected_output: Should give the McCormick linearization for binary-times-continuous: introduce z with the same [0,200] bounds and the four constraints (z>=lb*b, z<=ub*b, z>=x-ub*(1-b), z<=x-lb*(1-b)), with correct gurobipy code. Should note the bounds must be finite and tight (200 is fine here) and that if x were unbounded above an indicator (b==0)>>(x==0) is the right tool instead. Should explain the implicit Big-M is the bound (200), already tight, so no 1e6 needed.
assertions: Recognizes b*x is a binary-times-continuous product and gives the McCormick 4-constraint linearization (not a raw nonlinear z==b*x)
Provides correct gurobipy code with z bounded to x's range and the four addConstr lines
States the bounds must be finite/tight and that the effective Big-M is x's bound (200), so no arbitrary 1e6 is needed
Mentions the indicator-constraint alternative (b==0)>>(x==0) for the unbounded case
